name: Bonemaxxing guide

lead: Bonemaxxing is the looksmaxxing label for trying to improve bone structure, especially the face, without surgery. Followers aim for a stronger-looking jaw, cheekbones and frame, which they associate with a more defined appearance.

Guides typically list a small set of pillars such as testosterone, DHT and IGF-1 optimisation, micronutrients, sleep and bonesmashing. Forum members themselves debate whether bonemaxxing is real, and no published trial has tested these routines as a package for changing adult facial bone.

paras: A representative forum routine consists of five items: raising testosterone, DHT and IGF-1 through lifestyle means, getting enough micronutrients such as zinc, sleeping well, and bonesmashing. Posters describe updating such routines monthly and seeking feedback from others.

Bonesmashing involves striking facial bones and has injury risk. Hormone-oriented routines may involve compounds with medical risks, and commenters note that heavy training schedules can raise cortisol. People with open growth plates are in a different situation from adults.

chain: Load bone through practices such as bonesmashing
angle.text: Bonemaxxing guides aim at a more defined facial skeleton by combining growth-related hormones, nutrition, sleep and mechanical loading. Followers track photos monthly to judge changes.

lead: Bonemaxxing guide refers to forum-written plans for improving bone structure at home, the skeletal counterpart of softmaxxing practices such as skincare or leanness. Its goal is facial and frame structure: more prominent cheekbones, a sharper jaw, and a broader or taller frame. [1]

One looksmax.org post titled "My Bonemaxxing Methods" frames the routine as five main elements: testmaxxing, dhtmaxxing, IGF-1maxxing, sleep and bonesmashing. The author explains that testosterone and DHT matter for bone growth and remodelling especially during puberty, that micronutrients such as zinc support this, and that IGF-1 is also involved. [1]

The post is meant to be linked in the author's monthly updates, and a reply questioned whether the many sports in the routine would raise cortisol. [1] A separate thread asks whether bonemaxxing is real at all, showing the topic is contested within the community. [2] Mechanical-loading biology, summarised as Wolff's law, holds that bone adapts to the loads placed on it, which proponents cite as a rationale. [3]

paras: Guides generally present bonemaxxing as a bundle of natural levers. In the routine described on looksmax.org, the pillars are testosterone, DHT, IGF-1, sleep and bonesmashing, with micronutrients treated as part of healthy growth at any age. [1]

Proponents reason that hormones active in puberty drive bone growth and remodelling, so supporting them may influence structure; the cited post says results can be seen at any age but that puberty is the key period. [1] Mechanical loading is also invoked: general bone physiology holds that bone remodels in response to load, with examples such as stronger racquet-arm bones in tennis players. [3]
Within the community the topic is questioned. A thread titled "Is bonemaxxing real ?" exists, and replies to routine posts raise issues such as cortisol from overtraining. [1][2]

No studies found on bonemaxxing routines. Related research describes bone remodelling under mechanical load in the skeleton generally, which is not specific to facial bone change from these routines. [3]

lore.intro: Bonemaxxing guides circulate as personal routine posts on looksmax.org. [1][2]

claims.claim: Optimising testosterone, DHT and IGF-1 supports bone growth and remodelling
